provenance: Synthetic example written by Claude for development. The reference marks are Claude's, not a teacher's. Replace with teacher-marked work before quoting agreement figures.
title: Descriptive writing: a winter market
subject: English
schemeText:
Task: Describe a busy market on a winter morning. (10)
Content and organisation (4): 4 clear focus, well structured, paragraphs build a sense of place; 3 mostly focused with some structure; 2 some relevant ideas, limited structure; 1 few relevant ideas; 0 nothing relevant.
Language and imagery (4): 4 ambitious vocabulary and varied imagery used deliberately; 3 some effective imagery and well-chosen words; 2 some descriptive words, simple imagery; 1 basic vocabulary; 0 nothing creditable.
Accuracy (2): 2 spelling, punctuation and grammar mostly accurate with varied sentences; 1 errors that do not obscure meaning; 0 errors obscure meaning.
pupilWork: the market was very busy and cold. there was alot of people buying things and the stalls had food and clothes and toys. It was freezing and i was cold so we got hot chocolate it was nice. there was a man selling fish and it smelt bad. we stayed for a hour and then went home because my mum said so.

reference.notes: Some relevant ideas but drifts into narrative; simple descriptive words; capital letters and run-on sentences, but meaning clear.

demoResult.feedback: You picked out details from all the senses, such as the smell of the fish stall. Next, slow down and describe one part of the market closely, using capital letters to start each sentence.

criteria.evidence: we stayed for a hour and then went home
criteria.comment: Relevant ideas but becomes a recount; limited structure.

criteria.evidence: i was cold so we got hot chocolate it was nice
criteria.comment: Missing capitals and run-on sentences; meaning clear.
